To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the structure of field aligned currents in the cusp is more often filamentary than planar at the spatial resolution of Cluster (80 km) and that the current density is mainly carried by energetic electrons.

(1) the structure of the field-aligned current is more often filamentary than plane-like, (2) the parallel current is mostly carried by electrons, (3) ions are responsible for 20% of the parallel current and (4) the magnetic current density is not systematically larger than the particle current density

the structure of the field-aligned currents is more often filamentary than planar, and that in the plane current sheets the magnetic and particle currents are not in balance, the particle current being smaller than the magnetic one by a factor 2 to 4.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structure of currents and the transport of magnetosheaths plasmas in the cusp.
the study of the structure and of the particle current contribution to field-aligned current sheets associated with magnetosheath plasmas injections in the mid-altitudes cusp.
the study of the structure of the field-aligned currents in a region where the plasma sheet is not present.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the cusp is a complex system where filamentary and plane current structures coexist and interact, and that the parallel currents are mainly carried by electrons.
the cusp is a region where the magnetic field and the plasma are strongly coupled, but not in a simple way.
the cusp is a complex region where field-aligned currents are not systematically plane, and where the ratio between magnetic field and particle currents is not constant, even in plane current sheets.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the current density is not a well defined quantity, and that it should be treated with care.
the structure of field aligned currents is more often filamentary than plane, and the current sheets are not always oriented east-west.
the cusp is a very complex region where field-aligned currents can have a filamentary or sheet-like structure and where the current density can vary by a factor of 2 or 3 in a plane current sheet.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cusp at mid-latitudes is a complex structure where the field-aligned currents are not necessarily plane and where the parallel current is carried by electrons as well as by ions.
the current density deduced from magnetic measurements is a good approximation of the true current density in the mid-altitudinal cusp.
the structure of field aligned currents is more complex than previously thought.
